title: Salt and Thorn
premise: Gideon Vane, exiled for refusing to weaponize his storm-calling against a border village, survives by guiding smugglers through the Thornfell mountains. When a dying courier presses a bloodstained map into his hands, Gideon discovers the map charts the Seams—failing passages between the human realm and the thorn-bound Fae wilds—and that someone at court is deliberately severing them to hoard their magic. Hunted by the court's blade-witch Serah Kell and shadowed by Wren, the courier's daughter who wants the truth more than vengeance, Gideon must reach the First Seam and reforge the covenant his own family helped break generations ago. In the end Gideon sacrifices his exile's freedom—and nearly his life—to bind the Seams open, choosing truth over loyalty to the crown that banished him, while Wren chooses him over her duty of revenge.
about_author: K. M. Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former cartographer's apprentice who spent a decade mapping mountain passes before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about borders—geographic, moral, and emotional—from a cabin at the edge of a real forest that may or may not have thorns in it.

chapters.title: The Courier's Last Mile
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. Leading a smuggling run through Thornfell, Gideon finds a mortally wounded stranger who presses a bloodstained map into his hands with a warning: 'The Seams are closing.' The man dies as court riders crest the ridge. Emotional beat: reluctant inheritance—Gideon wanted no part of anyone's war, and now carries one.

chapters.title: What the Map Refuses to Show
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. Studying the map in a smuggler's den, Gideon recognizes his father's handwriting on its margins—proof his disgraced family was tied to the covenant. Court agents burn the den searching for it; he escapes through a hidden pass only he knows. Emotional beat: old wounds reopened; exile becomes personal again.

chapters.title: Wren of the Ash Road
chapters.summary: POV Wren. The dead courier's daughter ambushes Gideon on the Ash Road, certain he murdered her father. A fight ends in stalemate when she sees the map—and her father's seal. She demands to come along. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into purpose; enemies bound by shared loss.

chapters.title: The Village That Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. Sheltering in the border village Gideon once refused to attack, he learns the Seams' closing is already killing crops and memory itself—the villagers forget names overnight. Serah Kell arrives offering Gideon pardon for the map. He refuses. Emotional beat: temptation of forgiveness versus doing what's right.

chapters.title: Thornlight
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Crossing into the Fae wilds through a dying Seam, Wren negotiates passage with a thorn-lord who knew Gideon's father. She learns the covenant was broken deliberately—by human hands, perhaps Vane hands. Emotional beat: Wren's certainty cracks; the enemy may be the man beside her.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. Captured by Serah Kell, Gideon bargains with evidence: the court's Lord Chancellor has been harvesting Seam-magic to make himself unaging. Serah, herself sustained by stolen power, lets him go rather than face her own complicity. Emotional beat: power's corruption made flesh; even hunters are prisoners.

chapters.title: Where Loyalty Breaks
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Confronting Gideon with the ledger's implication that his father broke the covenant first, Wren draws steel—but he shows her the final page: his father signed it under duress to save the very village Gideon later refused to burn. Emotional beat: love against duty; Wren chooses trust over vengeance.

chapters.title: The Chancellor's Garden
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. Infiltrating the Chancellor's estate, they find a garden grown from a captive Seam, blooming on drained lifeforce. The Chancellor offers Gideon restoration of name and home in exchange for the map. Emotional beat: everything Gideon lost, offered back—at the cost of everyone else.

chapters.title: Storm Over the First Seam
chapters.summary: POV Gideon and Wren. At the First Seam, the Chancellor's ritual nears completion. Gideon calls a storm for the first time since his exile, tearing the garden's magic loose while Wren holds the binding circle against Serah Kell—who finally turns her blade on the Chancellor. Emotional beat: climax; sacrifice, fury, and unexpected alliance.

chapters.title: Salt and Thorn
chapters.summary: POV Wren. The covenant reforged, the Seams breathe open again, but the price stands: Gideon's storm-gift is spent, and the Fae require a mortal warden at the border. Wren takes the wardenship; Gideon, nameless but free, stays beside her. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—love chosen freely, duty transformed rather than abandoned.
